block.comment: Purpose: Explore local/global variable scope and a two-dimensional array. Hardware: use Connections to check pin ownership for your selected board. Open the comment bubbles on the main steps for explanations.
Replace one array element at the given indices. Indices start at zero and must stay below each declared dimension. Other elements keep their previous values.
Create column as int. Outside a body it is global; inside a function/setup/loop it belongs to that body. Its value input is the initial value.
Create row as int. Outside a body it is global; inside a function/setup/loop it belongs to that body. Its value input is the initial value.
Define writeSample once and call it elsewhere. It does not run just because it is defined. Arguments and variables declared inside this body are local.
Run the blocks inside this named function, then continue with the next block here. Reuse functions for repeated actions instead of copying their blocks.
Runs once after power-on or reset. Initialise the program here; repeating measurements and animation belong in loop.
Read one element using the current index values. This does not copy the whole array. Keep each index inside the corresponding dimension.
Wait for the given number of milliseconds (1000 ms = 1 second). This pauses the main program; avoid long waits when loop must service motors, music files or serial input.
Send this value/text to the computer. A new line finishes one record; same line can build a record from several values. Match Monitor/Plotter baud to the sketch.
Repeats until power is removed. Each block runs in order, then execution returns to the top. Keep this loop responsive when servicing motors, music or serial input.
